HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
HON’BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MR. G. NARENDAR
AND 
HON’BLE SRI JUSTICE ASHISH NAITHANI
31ST JULY, 2025
SPECIAL APPEAL NO. 110 OF 2025
Surendra Chandra ....Appellant
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others …..Respondents
WITH
SPECIAL APPEAL NO. 366 OF 2024
SPECIAL APPEAL NO. 368 OF 2024
SPECIAL APPEAL NO. 370 OF 2024
SPECIAL APPEAL NO. 371 OF 2024
SPECIAL APPEAL NO. 23 OF 2025
Counsel for the Appellants : Mr. Anil Anthwal and Mr. Lalit 
Samant and Ms. Ruchika Negi, 
learned counsels.
Counsel for the State : Mr. P.C. Bisht and Mr. B.S. Parihar, 
learned Additional Chief Standing 
Counsels with Mr. S.M.S. Mehta, 
learned Brief Holder. 
COMMON JUDGMENT :(per Mr. G. Narendar, C.J.)
Delay Condonation Applications (IA Nos.01/2024 and 01/2025)
For the reasons stated in the Applications seeking 
condonation of delay, the delay in preferring the aforementioned 
Special Appeals is condoned. Accordingly, the Applications (IA 
Nos.01 and 2024 and 01 of 2025) seeking condonation of delay, 
stand allowed.
2. So far as the above special appeals are concerned, it 
is seen that the basis for termination of the petitioners’/ 
appellants’ services, is the letter dated 25.05.2018, issued by 
the Chaudhary Charan Singh University, Meerut, which has 
stated that B.Ed. degree/ mark-sheet does not tally with the 
enrolment and confidential record maintained by the said 
University. In the absence of challenge to this foundational fact, 
1 2025:UHC:6816-DB
we are unable to comprehend as to how any relief can be
granted to a consequential order of removal which, admittedly, 
is premised on the opinion of the University.
3. It is also not in dispute that the letter was issued 
pursuant to the inquiry by the Special Investigation Team 
constituted for unearthing such unjustified/ illegal 
appointments.
4. In that view, learned counsels for the appellants pray 
leave to withdraw the instant special appeals with liberty to file 
fresh petitions calling in question the letter of the University 
dated 25.05.2018.
5. Reserving such liberty, the special appeals are 
dismissed as withdrawn.
6. There shall be no order as to costs. 
7. Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of 
accordingly. 
________________
G. NARENDAR, C.J.
 ________________
ASHISH NAITHANI, J.
Dated: 31st July, 2025
NISHANT
2

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
(Delay Condonation Appl. No.03 of 2025)
(Recall Appl. No.04 of 2025)
In
SPA No.110 of 2025
Surendra Chandra
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and others 
HON’BLE MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA, C.J.
HON’BLE ASHISH NAITHANI, J.
Mr. Anil Anthwal, learned counsel for the 
Appellant.
2. Mr. B.S. Parihar, Addl. Chief Standing Counsel 
and Mr. B.P.S. Mer, learned Standing Counsel for 
the State.
3. Heard on Delay Condonation Application.
4. There is delay of 202 days in filing the recall 
application. The delay has been sufficiently 
explained and is hereby condoned. Accordingly, 
delay condonation application is allowed. 
5. The recall application is accordingly taken up 
for consideration. 
6. The submission of learned counsel for the 
appellant is that the order of this Court, dismissing 
the appeal, but with liberty to the appellant to 
challenge the letter of the University dated
25.05.2018, on the basis of which the services of 
the appellant was terminated, would not serve any  purpose as the order of learned Single Judge, under 
challenge, against the termination order thereby 
stands upheld. It is submitted that the learned 
Single Judge has decided the bunch of writ petitions 
by a common order and judgment dated 03.10.2024 
and against which separate special appeals were 
filed by aggrieved persons. 
7. It is pointed out that one of such appeals being 
Special Appeal No.52 of 2025 filed by Smt. Kakuli
Mandal has been allowed by the Coordinate Division 
Bench vide judgment dated 31.07.2025 and the said 
judgment has also been upheld by the Hon’ble 
Supreme Court by dismissing the Special Leave 
Petition vide order dated 16.04.2026. 
8. The contention appears to have force, as in 
case the appeal is not heard and decided on merits, 
the order of learned Single Judge, dismissing the 
challenge to the order of termination of services of 
the appellant, would attain finality and any separate 
challenge made by the appellant in pursuance of 
liberty granted by this Court before the learned 
Single Judge would not serve any purpose. 
Accordingly, recall application is allowed. Order 
dated 31.07.2025 is hereby recalled. 
9. The special appeal shall be listed for hearing 
before the appropriate Bench as per Roster. 
(Ashish Naithani, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, C.J.)
